sentences.text: With the consent of the parties, heard finally at motion stage.

2.This appeal has been filed by the appellant under Section 173 (1) of Motor Vehicle Act, 1973 against the award dated 6.8.2022 passed in MACC No.16/2022 by Member, MACT, Narsinghpur seeking setting aside of impugned award and for grant of suitable compensation.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant, after referring to Ex.P/6, submits that Tribunal has wrongly dismissed the claim petition of the appellant on the ground that FIR has not been lodged immediately after the incident and it is delayed and there is no explanation for the same.
It is also urged that facts mentioned in Ex.P/6 have not been told by injured Keerat Patel, instead, same has been mentioned on the basis of information provided by Santosh.

Therefore, on the basis of Ex.P/6,
it cannot be said that appellant had not sustained injuries in accident and he fell from the motorcycle and thereafter, sustained injuries.
Learned counsel for the appellant after relying upon MA No.2853/2018 decided on 22.12.2023 submits that a claim petition cannot be dismissed on the ground of delay in lodging the FIR.

It is also urged that non- applicant no. 1 and 2 driver and owner of offending vehicle did not cross- examine the applicant witness Chironjilal Patel and it is not the case of the non- applicant no. 1 and 2 that they/their vehicle has been falsely implicated in the accident.
Therefore, it is urged that learned tribunal has wrongly dismissed the claim petition of the appellant.
Hence, appeal filed by the appellant be allowed and impugned award be set aside and appropriate compensation be awarded.
4. Learned counsel for the respondents submits that Tribunal after taking into consideration overall evidence on record, has rightly dismissed the claim of the petitioner.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
6. It is correct that claim petition cannot be dismissed solely on the ground of delay in lodging the FIR.

In the instant case, accident occurred on 6.12.2020 and FIR Ex.P/2 has been registered after enquiry on 3.1.2021.
7.
Perusal of depositions of appellant Keerat Patel and discharge ticket Ex.P/20 reveals that appellant has been discharged from hospital on 14.12.2020.

Thus, in the instant case, neither appellant/injured Keerat Patel nor eye witness Chironjilal has lodged FIR, mentioning the registration number of the offending vehicle immediately after the accident or after discharge from the hospital on 14.12.2020 and no explanation, whatsoever, has been furnished for the same.

In view of above fact, owner and driver did not cross-examine applicant witness Chironjilal or they did not specifically mentioned that they have been falsely implicated in the case, it does not establish that present accidnet occurred from the offending vehicle.
8. Further, in Ex.P/16, it is mentioned that injured has sustained injuries on account of fall from the motorcycle/vehicle.
Ex.P/5 is of 22.12.2020 and therein also, no registration number of offending vehicle has been mentioned.

2 9.
Hence, in view of discussion in the forgoing paras, principle of law laid down in the case of Union of India (Supra) do not apply to the facts of the present case.
10. Hence, in view of discussion in the forgoing paras, findings recorded by the Tribunal in para 14 cannot be said to be perverse or against the evidence on record.
Hence, no interference is required in the findings recorded by the Tribunal.
11. Accordingly, appeal filed by the appellant is dismissed.

(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE Hashmi Keerat Patel vs Maneesh Goswami on 13 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23677638/
